title: Who does the Perception gap video work for?
rationale: The Perception gap video lowered affective polarization by 2.3 points (95% CI [-4.3, -0.4], n=641 vs control 229), but exploratory party and interest interactions were null with intervals of about ±7 points. A dedicated, stratified, powered test is needed to learn whether the effect depends on partisanship, political interest or baseline misperception.
contribution: Provides a preregistered, powered test of three moderators of the Perception gap video effect on affective polarization.
limitations: Interaction power depends on the assumed SE; true heterogeneity may be smaller than detectable.
Immediate outcomes only; durability is unknown.
Pre-treatment misperception measurement may itself prime respondents and weaken the treatment.
Quota panel is not truly probability-based.

design.title: Moderators of the Perception gap video effect
design.overview: US adults from a quota panel, with Lucid as a supplementary source, are stratified by party (Democrat/Republican, leaners included) and political interest (high/low). Respondents complete pre-treatment thermometers and an out-party misperception measure, then are randomized to the Perception gap video or a control. Post-treatment thermometers follow. Three interactions are preregistered: treatment x party, treatment x interest, treatment x baseline misperception.
design.hypothesis: The video effect on affective polarization is larger (more negative) for respondents with larger baseline misperception; effects of party and interest are tested as two-sided preregistered interactions.
design.primaryOutcome: Affective polarization: in-party minus out-party feeling thermometer after treatment.
design.comparison: Video vs control, with treatment x party, treatment x political interest and treatment x baseline misperception interactions, adjusted for pre-treatment polarization.
design.population: US adults identifying as Democrat or Republican (including leaners), recruited from a quota panel plus Lucid, with quotas on party and political interest.

conditions.title: Perception gap video
conditions.description: The Perception gap video with misperception data, as in the source study.

questions.text: You are invited to take part in a research study on political attitudes. It takes about 10 minutes and participation is voluntary. Do you consent to participate?
Generally speaking, do you usually think of yourself as a Republican, a Democrat, an Independent, or something else?
Do you think of yourself as closer to the Republican Party or to the Democratic Party?
Generally, how interested are you in politics?
Please rate each group on a feeling thermometer from 0 (cold, unfavorable) to 100 (warm, favorable). Choose the point closest to your feeling.
Out of every 100 members of the other party, how many do you think would say that the other side is not just wrong but a threat to the country?
Please watch the following video carefully. {{ed:video1}}
What did you just see, read, or watch?

choices.text: A video about how we misperceive the other party

questions.text: Please rate each group on a feeling thermometer from 0 (cold, unfavorable) to 100 (warm, favorable). Choose the point closest to your feeling.

Thank you. This study examined how information about the other party affects political attitudes. The video described how Americans often overestimate the other party's hostility. Contact the research team with any questions.
Thank you for your time. You did not consent, so the survey ends here.

flow.label: Video stimulus
flow.value: [VIDEO: Perception gap video showing how Democrats and Republicans overestimate each other's hostility, about 6 minutes]

assumptions: Power: about 1200 per arm (about 2400 total) to detect a 2.5-point main effect at 80% power; interaction SEs of 3-3.6 at source arm sizes mean interaction MDEs need about 4x the n of the main effect.
Thermometers are collected as 5 binned points because the schema has no slider type; a slider implementation on the platform is preferable and should replace the bins.
Quotas: equal numbers of Democrats and Republicans, and high/low interest cells (extremely/very vs lower) approximately balanced.
Platform: a quota panel (probability-based if available) plus Lucid, with panel source recorded and controlled for.
Three interactions preregistered with Holm correction; baseline misperception is mean-centered.
Compensation set at the panel standard for a 10-minute survey.
unresolved: The actual Perception gap video file must be supplied and hosted by the research team.
IRB approval number and compensation details must be supplied by the research team.
The panel vendor and quota feasibility for 2400 respondents must be confirmed.
